description: Project Overview This is a comprehensive, interactive data dashboard I developed to visualize and analyze the budget performance of 47 counties in Kenya for the financial year 2023/24. The project transforms complex public financial data from the Office of the Controller of Budget into an accessible, interactive web application. Key Features: Interactive Map Visualization -Choropleth map with color-coded counties based on key performance metrics -Dual-layer visualization (polygon boundaries + circle markers) for flexible data exploration -Popup information windows displaying detailed county-specific data -Custom legend system adapting to different metrics Multi-Metric Analysis: The dashboard tracks six key performance indicators: -Overall absorption rate -Development absorption rate -Revenue performance -Wage bill as percentage of revenue -Pending bills (in Kshs. Billion) -Total budget allocation Comprehensive Dashboard Tabs: -Performance Analysis: Top-performing counties and budget allocation patterns -County Comparison: Side-by-side radar chart comparison of any two counties -Trend Analysis: Historical performance trends over five years -Revenue Analysis: Revenue sources breakdown and own-source revenue leaders -Efficiency Metrics: Scatter plot matrices showing absorption vs. revenue performance Interactive Controls: .Metric selector to change map coloring .Region and county filters .Year selector for trend analysis .Layer toggles for map visualization control Data export functionality (CSV) Technical Implementation Frontend Technologies Leaflet.js for interactive mapping with custom GeoJSON integration Chart.js and D3.js for all data visualizations (bar charts, doughnut charts, scatter plots, radar charts, line graphs) PapaParse for CSV data handling HTML5/CSS3 with responsive design principles Data Architecture 47 Kenyan counties with 15+ data points each GeoJSON boundary data integrated with county-level metrics Regional aggregation for comparative analysis Historical trend data spanning 5 financial years Key Insights Delivered The dashboard reveals critical patterns in Kenya's county financial management: Significant variation in budget absorption rates (64.7% to 90.8%) Heavy dependency on national government transfers (72% of revenue) Wage bill pressures exceeding legal limits in multiple counties Development expenditure lagging at only 24.4% of total spending Pending bills exceeding Kshs. 181 billion overall Impact & Value: This tool serves multiple stakeholders: -Government officials can identify underperforming counties and best practices -Citizens gain transparency into public fund utilization -Researchers access clean, visualizable financial data -Policymakers can make data-driven resource allocation decisions

title: Kenya Disability Dashboard
description:
PRIJECT OVERVIEW:
This is an interactive data visualization dashboard that analyzes disability statistics from the 2019 Kenya Population and Housing Census. It transforms raw census data into an accessible, map-based tool that helps users understand disability prevalence across Kenya's 47 counties.
The Problem This Solves:
Before this dashboard, disability data was buried in lengthy PDF reports and complex spreadsheets. Policymakers, researchers, and advocates couldn't easily:
See which counties have the highest disability rates
Compare different types of disabilities (mobility vs. vision vs. hearing)
Identify regional patterns or clusters
Export insights for reports or presentations.
FEATURES:
1. Interactive County Map
Color-coded map of Kenya showing disability rates by county-Click any county to see its specific data
 Dynamic updating as you filter or select different disability types

2. Six Disability Domains Analyzed
Domain-	What It Measures
Mobility-	Difficulty walking or climbing stairs
Seeing-	Difficulty with vision even with glasses
Hearing-	Difficulty with hearing even with hearing aid
Cognition-	Difficulty remembering or concentrating
Self-Care-	Difficulty with daily self-care activities
Communication-	Difficulty being understood or understanding others
3. Analytical Tools
Spatial Filtering: Select multiple counties to focus analysis on specific regions
Domain Comparison: Compare two disability types against each other
Clustering Analysis: Groups counties with similar disability patterns
Correlation Matrix: Shows relationships between different disability types

4. Export Capabilities
Export maps as PNG images
Download data as CSV files
Generate PDF analysis reports


Who Would Use This:
User	Use Case
Government policymakers	Resource allocation and planning
NGOs and disability advocates	Identifying underserved regions
Researchers and academics	Statistical analysis and trend identification
Healthcare planners	Service delivery targeting
Journalists	Data-driven reporting
Technical Implementation:
The dashboard is built as a single HTML file using:

Leaflet.js for interactive mapping

D3.js for data visualizations and charts

Chart.js for additional charting capabilities

jsPDF & html2canvas for PDF/PNG export functionality

Data is embedded as GeoJSON with county boundaries and census statistics for all 47 Kenyan counties.

VALUE PROPOSITIO
This dashboard transforms static census numbers into an actionable tool for understanding disability in Kenya. It makes complex data accessible, comparable, and exportable — saving hours of manual data processing and enabling evidence-based decision making.

projects.title: Kenya Multi-Year Diaspora Remitance Flow
projects.description: PROJECT OVERVIEW: The Project maps remittance flows from six world regions — North America, Europe, Middle East, Africa, Asia-Pacific, and Rest of World — into Kenya using animated curved lines on a Leaflet map. The line thickness, color, and animation speed represent the remittance amount, while tooltips and popups show exact values and distances. KEY FEATURES: Yearly data views -Switch between 2022–2025 to see remittance changes over time Region filtering-Focus on a single region’s flows Dynamic map styling- Line width scales with remittance value; colors by region Animated flows- Dashed lines with pulsing/moving effects to indicate direction and scale Statistics panel- Shows total remittance per region and average distance traveled Trend analysis- Line chart and YoY growth table with market share Data export -Export as GeoJSON, CSV, or plain-text analysis report Responsive design-Works on desktop and mobile screen. VALUE IT BRINGS: 1. For Policy Makers & Economists Quickly identify which diaspora regions contribute most to Kenya’s foreign exchange. Track year-over-year growth trends to guide foreign policy, trade agreements, or diaspora engagement programs. Understand geographic concentration of remittances for targeted financial inclusion initiatives. 2. For Financial Institutions & Remittance Companies Spot high-value corridors (e.g., North America, Europe) for marketing and fee reduction strategies. Analyze market share by region to prioritize expansion or partnerships. Use exported data for internal forecasting and reporting. 3. For Researchers Study spatial patterns of global migration and its economic impact. Access a clean, reusable dataset (GeoJSON/CSV) for further analysis in GIS tools like QGIS or ArcGIS. Understand how distance correlates with remittance volume (though not causal, it’s visualized). 4. For Data Storytellers & Journalists Embed the interactive map in articles or reports about Kenya’s economy. Use the trend charts to visually communicate growth stories (e.g., “Middle East remittances grew 8% in 2024”). 5. Technical Value Demonstrates integration of Leaflet + Turf.js for geodesic line calculation and spatial analysis. Shows real-time filtering, animation toggling, and data persistence without a backend. Serves as a template for any origin-destination flow mapping project (trade, migration, internet traffic, etc.). TECHNOLOGY: Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (vanilla) Mapping: Leaflet.js + CartoDB basemap Geospatial math: Turf.js (distance, midpoint, bounding box, geodesic interpolation) Charts: Chart.js Data storage: localStorage (can be extended to Mavo or a real API) Animations: CSS keyframes (flow-pulse, flow-move) Bottom Line This project transforms static remittance numbers into an interactive, geographic story — helping anyone from government analysts to journalists see where money flows from, how much, and whether it’s growing — all in a self-contained, no-backend web app.
